lead: Each story names who, what, and why. Open one for confirmation and the walk.

items.name: Portfolio
items.statusNote: The live prototype already walks this.
items.summary: See use across the estate, a group, or a site.
items.who: A Customer uses Portfolio. Viewer can look. Contributor can work.

sections.name: Tree
sections.summary: Find and pick a place on the estate

sections.name: Consumption
sections.summary: Read use on the graph for a group or a site

sections.name: Site profile
sections.summary: See and set hours, time of use, and attributes for each site and meter

stories.name: Scan the estate
stories.want: see All and the named groups on the tree
stories.benefit: I can start from the collective before I pick a place
stories.notes: This is the first look at Portfolio. Tabs other than Consumption wait for their own stories.

criteria.then: All sits at the top with a grey site count
I see the collective overview
its sites show and other groups hide
its sites hide

stages.name: All on the tree
stages.caption: All sits at the top. The pane is the collective overview.

stages.name: A group open
stages.caption: The group shows its sites. Opening one group closes the others.

estimate.why: More than Search. Tree, All, and group accordion.

stories.name: Find a site or meter
stories.want: search for a site or meter
stories.benefit: I can reach it without walking the whole tree
stories.notes: Filter sits to the right. Filter behaviour sits on Filter the tree.

criteria.when: I look at the search field
criteria.then: the label is Search site or meter
matching sites sit in the tree
Search starts again

stages.name: Search the tree
stages.caption: Type a site or meter. Hits sit in the tree.

estimate.why: This is the 2. Search, then hits in the tree.

stories.name: Filter the tree
stories.want: tick ownership, meter, and In or Out
stories.benefit: the tree only shows places that match
stories.notes: The same ticks sit on the pane Filter, to the right of Compare. Water on is Tick Water.

criteria.given: I open Filter on the tree
criteria.then: I can tick Electricity, Gas, Water, In, and Out
Water is off
pills sit there and the Filter count is a cyan circle with no black rim

criteria.when: I use the cross or Clear
criteria.then: that one goes, or they all go

stages.name: Filter overlay
stages.caption: Ticks for Ownership, Meter, and Incoming and Outgoing.

stages.name: Filter pills
stages.caption: Pills sit under Search. A cross clears that one.

estimate.why: Overlay ticks, pills, count, and Clear.

stories.name: Read a group
stories.want: see consumption for a group
stories.benefit: I can read the collective without opening each site
stories.notes: Cost, Carbon, Site profile, Alerts, and Queries are other stories. Pills on the group are sites.

criteria.then: the kicker is the company and the heading is the group
the graph is the collective for the sites that are on

criteria.given: site pills sit above the tabs
criteria.then: that site leaves the graph, and I can take the last one off

stages.name: Group pane
stages.caption: Collective consumption. Each pill is a site.

estimate.why: Collective graph and site pills.

stories.name: Read a site
stories.want: see Incoming and Outgoing on a site
stories.benefit: import and export share one graph
stories.notes: Do not put All, In, or Out chips on the site head. Do not put a meter Select on the site head.

criteria.given: I open a site with both channels
criteria.then: the title is Incoming and outgoing
In is cyan with an import mark and Out is black with an export mark

criteria.given: In and Out pills sit under the graph
criteria.then: that series leaves, the name strikes through, and I can take the last one off
each pill is a meter, even if there is only one

stages.name: Site pane
stages.caption: Incoming and outgoing. In is cyan. Out is black.

estimate.why: Incoming and Outgoing, the key, and meter pills.

stories.name: Change the window
stories.want: change the date window
stories.benefit: I can read a preset or a custom from and to
stories.notes: Gaps stay gaps. Zero is a reading.

criteria.then: I can pick Last 24 hours, Last 7 days, Last month, Last 12 months, or Custom
I set from and to, and the title uses those dates
the window moves and the filter becomes Custom, then the preset again at the original window

stages.name: Date on the graph
stages.caption: The preset name sits next to the title. Arrows sit to the right.

estimate.why: Date Select, Custom calendar, and arrows.

stories.name: Switch the graph
stories.want: switch Total or Individual, and Bar or Line
stories.benefit: I can add readings up or break them down, and pick a graph style
stories.notes: Cost and Carbon are their own stories. Incoming and Outgoing stay cyan and black bars when Total and Bar are on.

criteria.then: the graph adds the readings up as bars
I see one line per site
I see one line per meter
I see one line for the total

stages.name: Individual consumption
stages.caption: Lines, one per site on a group, or one per meter on a site.

estimate.why: Bars or lines, and group vs site.

stories.name: See Cost
stories.want: see Cost for the same window
stories.benefit: I can read spend in pounds
stories.notes: Rates on Site profile feed the walk numbers. Water uses £.

criteria.given: I am on a group or a site
criteria.then: the title is Cost and the unit is £
I can pick Total cost or Individual cost

stages.name: Cost on the pane
stages.caption: Same window as Consumption. The unit is £.

estimate.why: Same graph as Consumption. The unit is £.

stories.name: See Carbon
stories.want: see Carbon for the same window
stories.benefit: I can read kgCO2e for the same places
stories.notes: Water uses the 2026 supply and wastewater factors, combined on the graph.

criteria.given: I am on a group or a site
criteria.then: the title is Carbon and the unit is kgCO2e
I can pick Total carbon or Individual carbon

stages.name: Carbon on the pane
stages.caption: Same window as Consumption. The unit is kgCO2e.

estimate.why: Same graph as Consumption. The unit is kgCO2e.

stories.name: Compare others
stories.want: compare others at this level
stories.benefit: I can add more than one place to the graph
stories.notes: On one meter, Compare lists other meters throughout the portfolio. The row is the site and the MPAN.

criteria.given: I am on a group or a site
criteria.then: a modal lists others at that level
I can add more than one
the count is a cyan circle with no black rim, and the cross clears it

stages.name: Compare modal
stages.caption: Search, Filter, and a list of others at that level.

estimate.why: Modal, more than one place, and lines on the graph.

stories.name: Compare site profiles
stories.want: see the hours, time of use, floor area, and occupants of every site in one table
stories.benefit: I can spot gaps across a group without opening each site
stories.notes: Shows on All and on a group. Download template sits with Upload above the table. Upload is its own story. Custom means hours or time of use set by hand with no saved preset.

criteria.given: I am on All or a group
criteria.then: a table lists each site with Operational hours, Time of use, Floor area, and Occupants
the tag shows the preset name, or Custom if no preset is saved

criteria.given: the meters on a site use different weeks
criteria.then: the tag reads Mixed

criteria.given: some days have no times, or no week is set
criteria.then: the tag reads Incomplete or Missing
I see each day of the week and its times
it holds the sites in the table, ready to fill in
I see Site profile for that site

stages.name: Sites table
stages.caption: One row per site. Download template and Upload sit above the table.

stages.name: Week on hover
stages.caption: Hover a tag to see each day of the week.

estimate.why: A table of sites, tags that fold many meters into one, week tips, and the template

stories.name: Read a site profile
stories.want: see where a site is and how its hours and time of use are set
stories.benefit: I can check a site at a glance before I change anything
stories.notes: Custom means hours or time of use set by hand with no saved preset. A preset on a meter shows its name and the icon for that meter's utility. Floor area and occupants sit under Attributes.

criteria.given: I click a site row, or pick a site on the tree
criteria.then: I see a map of the site and its address

criteria.given: hours or time of use are set by hand with no saved preset
criteria.then: it reads Custom

criteria.given: a meter uses a saved preset
criteria.then: it shows the preset name with the icon for that meter's utility

criteria.given: I hover a time of use tag such as Weekday peak
criteria.then: I see each day of the week with its on peak and off peak times

criteria.given: I hover an operational hours tag
criteria.then: I see each day of the week with its open hours
I can dig deeper into the settings for that site

stages.name: Site profile
stages.caption: The map, address, hours, time of use, and attributes. Site settings sits to the right.

stages.name: Week on hover
stages.caption: Hover a preset to see on peak and off peak for each day.

estimate.why: Map, address, and tags. The tip reuses the week tip from the sites table

stories.name: Read the meters on a site
stories.want: see each meter on a site with its channel, settings, last reading, and use
stories.benefit: I can tell which meters follow the site and which do not
stories.notes: From site means the meter takes the site settings, so three meters are set once, not three times. Change one meter and it becomes Custom. Do not invent a SPID.

criteria.given: I am on Site profile for a site
criteria.then: Meters lists each meter with Meter, Channel, Settings, Last reading, and Use
I see its number, such as the MPAN, with the icon for its utility
it reads In, Out, or both

criteria.given: a meter takes the site settings
criteria.then: it reads From site

criteria.given: a meter has its own settings
criteria.then: it reads Custom

criteria.when: I read Last reading and Use
criteria.then: I see when the last reading came in and how much the meter used
Site settings opens with Attributes on the tab for that meter's utility

stages.name: Meters
stages.caption: One row per meter, below the site.

estimate.why: Five columns. From site has to compare each meter with the site settings

stories.name: Open Site settings
stories.want: open the settings for a site
stories.benefit: I can change its hours, time of use, and attributes in one place
stories.notes: Each accordion has its own story. Upload is its own story. Viewers can read Site settings but cannot change it. The prototype shows no message after Save changes and no prompt when you leave with changes. Both are gaps to close before build.

criteria.given: I am on Site profile for a site
criteria.then: Operational hours, Time of use, and Attributes sit as closed accordions
the group and site name sit on the left, with Download template and Upload on the right
site-settings.csv holds Site, Meter point, Section, Group, Setting, Value, and Unit for every period and attribute on the site

criteria.given: a meter has its own settings
criteria.then: its lines follow the site lines under its meter point, and a blank meter point means the site

criteria.given: no meter on the site has times
criteria.then: it shows Missing

criteria.given: any day has a gap or a missing time
criteria.then: it shows Incomplete

criteria.given: the times are complete and some meters have their own
criteria.then: it shows Mixed
it is off

criteria.given: I have changed the site or any meter
criteria.then: the site and every changed meter save together

criteria.given: a period has an error or the site name is empty
criteria.then: it stays off until I fix it

criteria.given: a day has a gap but no error
criteria.then: it saves, since a gap is a warning
my changes are still there
I can read every setting but cannot change one, and Download template and Upload do not show

stages.name: Site settings
stages.caption: Three accordions. Download template and Upload sit at the top.

estimate.why: One save covers the site and every meter. Changes wait until saved. The template lists every setting

stories.name: Choose who the settings are for
stories.want: choose whether I set the whole site or one meter
stories.benefit: I set most meters once at the site and only change the ones that differ
stories.notes: Operational hours and Time of use each have their own Settings for. Picking a meter in one does not pick it in the other. Attributes have no Settings for, since they split into Site and utility tabs. The site has nothing to follow, so it has no source cards.

criteria.given: a site has two or more meters, or a meter has its own settings
criteria.when: I open Operational hours or Time of use
criteria.then: Settings for sits at the top with the site first, then each meter

criteria.given: a site has one meter and it follows the site
criteria.then: there is no Settings for and I set the site
the site reads Every meter that follows the site, and each meter shows its MPAN, MPRN, or serial, its utility, and From site or Custom
the times for each day show straight away, with no source cards
Follow Crewe depot and Set for this meter only sit as single-select cards
they match the site and are locked, with the tip These follow Crewe depot. Choose Set for this meter only to change them

criteria.when: I pick Set for this meter only
criteria.then: its times start as a copy of the site and I can change them

criteria.given: a meter has its own times
criteria.then: it drops its own times and takes the site times again

criteria.given: I followed the site by mistake before saving
criteria.when: I pick Set for this meter only again
criteria.then: the meter gets back the times I set
the meter changes with them

criteria.given: a meter has its own times
criteria.then: the meter keeps its own

criteria.given: I opened Site settings from a meter row
criteria.when: I open Operational hours or Time of use
criteria.then: that meter is already picked

criteria.given: I saved a meter with its own times
criteria.then: its Settings reads Custom, and From site again once it follows the site

stages.name: The site
stages.caption: The site is picked, so the times show with no source cards.

stages.name: A meter that follows
stages.caption: Follow Crewe depot is on, so the times are locked.

stages.name: A meter on its own
stages.caption: Set for this meter only is on, so the times can change.

estimate.why: Two parts with their own picker. Following and setting a meter on its own must not lose its times

stories.name: Set operational hours for each day
stories.want: set the operational hours for each day of the week
stories.benefit: Astral knows when the site is operational and when it is not
stories.notes: A day runs from 00:00 to 24:00. 24:00 is midnight at the end of the day. The talk named Operational and Non-operational. The prototype also has Closed, so confirm whether it stays. Gaps warn but do not stop the save. Errors stop it.

criteria.when: I look at Times for each day
criteria.then: Monday to Sunday sit as tabs above a table with Select preset, From, To, Status, and Remove
it shows the periods for that day only
one blank row shows with the note No times set for this day. Enter times or select a preset

criteria.given: I type in From or To
criteria.then: it takes 24-hour time such as 08:00, up to 24:00
I can choose Operational, Non-operational, or Closed

criteria.given: part of the day has no period
criteria.then: a new row fills the first gap with the opposite status to the period before it

criteria.given: periods cover the whole day up to 24:00
criteria.when: I look at Add a period
criteria.then: it is off with the tip This day is covered up to 24:00. Shorten a period to add another
it is off with the tip A day needs at least one period. Change this one instead

criteria.given: a day has more than one period
criteria.then: the row goes and leaves a gap I can fill

criteria.given: a period has no start or no end
criteria.then: I see Enter a start and end time for every period

criteria.given: a period ends at or before its start
criteria.then: I see Each period must end after it starts. Use 24:00 for midnight at the end of the day
I see Periods overlap from 09:00 to 10:00. Change one so each time sits in only one period

criteria.given: no period covers part of the day
criteria.then: I see No period covers 17:00 to 18:00. Add a period so the whole day is set
a red flag marks it

criteria.given: a day has a gap or no times
criteria.then: a yellow flag marks it
it stays off until I fix it

stages.name: Times for each day
stages.caption: Day tabs above the periods for one day.

stages.name: A period to fix
stages.caption: An overlap shows in red and flags the day tab.

estimate.why: Day tabs, a period table, Add a period, Remove, and three errors and two warnings

stories.name: Set time of use for each day
stories.want: set when each day is on peak and off peak
stories.benefit: Cost charges each hour at the right unit rate
stories.notes: Time of use works like operational hours, with the same tabs, table, buttons, and checks. It differs in its statuses, its presets, and what it feeds. Water has one unit rate, so time of use does not change its cost.

criteria.when: I look at Times for each day
criteria.then: the day tabs, table, Add a period, Remove, and checks work as in Operational hours
I can choose On peak or Off peak, with no Closed
I see On peak and off peak, Weekday peak, Night and day, and Off peak all day

criteria.given: I use a preset for a full week
criteria.then: I see Standard week, Weekday peak, and Night and day

criteria.given: On peak and Off peak are set
criteria.then: use in on-peak periods is charged at the On-peak unit rate in Attributes, and the rest at the Off-peak unit rate

criteria.given: a meter has its own time of use
criteria.then: its own periods decide the split
nothing has changed, since each has its own times and its own Settings for

stages.name: Time of use
stages.caption: On peak and Off peak periods for one day.

estimate.why: Reuses the day table. Cost must read the split for each hour

stories.name: Use a preset
stories.want: fill a week or a day from a preset
stories.benefit: I do not type the same times for every site
stories.notes: Standard presets come with Astral and suit many customers. Your presets belong to the company, so anyone in it can use them. A day that uses a preset follows it, so a later change to the preset reaches that day. Managing presets in Settings is its own story.

criteria.then: a modal asks me to choose A full week or One day
I see Your saved weeks, with company presets before standard ones
I see Your saved days, then choose the days to use it on, with the open day ticked

criteria.given: no presets of that kind exist
criteria.then: it reads No saved weeks yet or No saved days yet

criteria.given: I have not chosen a preset
criteria.then: it is off

criteria.given: I chose a day preset but ticked no days
criteria.then: it is off
all seven days take its times
only the ticked days take its times and the first of them opens

criteria.given: I want one day to use a preset
criteria.when: I open Select preset in the table
criteria.then: I see Custom, Standard presets, Your presets, and Manage presets

criteria.given: I pick a preset in Select preset
criteria.then: that day takes the times and statuses of the preset

criteria.when: I change one of its times
criteria.then: Select preset reads Custom

criteria.given: I changed a day that used a preset
criteria.then: I see Edited from Weekday peak with Undo, which puts the preset times back

criteria.given: a day reads Custom after I changed it
criteria.when: I type the preset times back
criteria.then: it links to the preset again
the times stay and the day stops following the preset
Settings opens on Presets
the day takes the new times

stages.name: Use a preset
stages.caption: Choose a full week or one day.

stages.name: Choose the days
stages.caption: A day preset asks which days to use it on.

stages.name: Select preset
stages.caption: Each day can pick a preset in the table.

estimate.why: A modal with up to three steps, plus a picker for each day. Days must stay linked to their preset

stories.name: Save a preset
stories.want: save the times I set as a preset
stories.benefit: my company can use them on other sites and meters
stories.notes: A preset is shared across the company. Updating one changes every site and meter that uses it, so the times never conflict. Standard presets cannot change. A match compares times and statuses, not names.

criteria.then: I choose A full week or One day, pick the day for one day, and enter a Preset name
it is off with the tip Enter times for at least one day to save them as a preset
I see Fix the periods marked in red to save
I see Enter a name for the preset
I see A preset with this name already exists. Enter a different name

criteria.given: the times match one preset I have
criteria.then: it asks Use Weekday peak? and says There is nothing new to save. To keep a copy under another name, save it as a new preset

criteria.given: the times match more than one preset
criteria.then: it asks Use a preset you already have? and marks each as Standard preset or Your preset

criteria.given: I changed a day after picking one of my presets
criteria.then: it asks Update Weekday peak? with Update preset, Save as new, and Cancel

criteria.given: other days or sites use that preset
criteria.then: it warns Updating Weekday peak also changes the times at Crewe depot, Euston, and 2 more sites
every day, site, and meter that uses the preset takes the new times
a new preset saves under my name and the day links to it

criteria.given: I changed a day after picking a standard preset
criteria.then: it says the standard preset cannot be changed and asks me to save my times as a new preset

criteria.when: I open Use a preset or Select preset
criteria.then: it sits under Your presets

stages.name: Save preset
stages.caption: Name the times as a full week or one day.

stages.name: Update a preset
stages.caption: A changed preset can update everywhere or save as new.

estimate.why: Matching, naming, and updating a shared preset that reaches other sites

stories.name: Set site attributes
stories.want: set the details of a site and the rates for each utility
stories.benefit: Cost, Carbon, and the site address read correctly
stories.notes: Attributes have no Settings for. For now a meter gets its own rates only by upload. Postcode has no format check. The Site ID never changes, so two sites can share a name.

criteria.then: Site comes first, then only the utilities the site has
I see Site name, Floor area in mÂ², Number of employees, Street name, Town or city, Postcode, and Country
it is locked with the hint Only admins can change the site name

criteria.given: I am an admin and clear Site name
criteria.then: I see Enter a site name and Save changes is off
I see Site capacity in kVA, Emissions factor in kgCO2e/kWh, Daily standing charge in Â£/day, and On-peak and Off-peak unit rates in p/kWh
I see the Electricity fields without Site capacity
I see Emissions factor in kgCO2e/mÂ³, Daily standing charge in Â£/day, and Unit rate in p/mÂ³

criteria.given: I opened Site settings from a meter row
criteria.then: it shows the tab for that meter's utility

criteria.given: a meter has its own rates
criteria.then: its own rates win over the site rates

stages.name: Attributes
stages.caption: Site first, then a tab for each utility on the site.

estimate.why: A tab per utility with fixed fields. Only the site name has a rule

stories.name: Tick Water
stories.want: tick Water
stories.benefit: I can read m³ on a site that holds a water meter
stories.notes: Walk sites hold a water meter so the tick has a hit. Dummy site A1 still holds one. Serial then the number. Gas is a flame. Water is a drop. Do not invent a SPID.

criteria.then: sites with water meters are hits, including Dummy site A1

criteria.given: I am on that site with Water on
criteria.then: the unit is m³

criteria.given: I am on Cost or Carbon
criteria.then: Cost is £ and Carbon is kgCO2e

criteria.given: Electricity, Gas, and Water are on from Cost
criteria.then: I see that this combination cannot be shown, and I can View water or View electricity & gas

stages.name: Water on Dummy site A1
stages.caption: The water mark is a drop. Use is m³.

estimate.why: New unit, Water off until ticked, and Dummy site A1.

estimate.help: Points are relative size, not days. Find a site or meter is the 2.
